diagnosis_explanation: Your brain was hurt during your injury. This can cause trouble with thinking or feeling. Your neck muscles are also sore. This may make your neck feel stiff or painful.
medication_rationale: Your doctor did not give you any new medicines to take at home. Ask at your next visit if you need to start any.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired and sore after your procedure.
- Focus on resting at home.
- Try short, slow walks around your house.
- Your goal is to walk for 5 minutes, 3 times a day.
- Call your doctor if you have a sudden, severe headache.
- Call your doctor if your neck pain gets much worse.

**Week 2:**
- You might feel a little more energy this week.
- Focus on gentle movements.
- Do the exercises from your home program.
- Avoid turning your head quickly.
- Your goal is to increase walking time by 5 minutes.
- Call your doctor if you feel dizzy or lose balance.

**Week 3:**
- You can start doing more light activities at home.
- Slowly increase the time you spend walking.
- Continue with your prescribed home exercises.
- Try to practice self-care tasks like dressing yourself.
- Your goal is to walk for 15 minutes, 2 times a day.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble remembering things.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel stronger and more comfortable.
- You can try light household chores, but avoid bending over.
- Continue increasing your walking distance gradually.
- Practice tasks that help you with daily living.
- Your goal is to walk for 20 minutes, 1 time a day.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worsening pain.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Many people feel better over the next 4 to 8 weeks.
- Keep doing your home exercises regularly.
- Listen to your body and do not push too hard.
- You will continue to regain strength and coordination.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Cannot breathe or gasping: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain that will not stop: Your heart needs help now.
- Loss of consciousness or fainting: Get help right away.
- Seizure: Call 911 right away.
- Signs of stroke: face drooping, arm weakness, trouble speaking: Get help right away.
- Uncontrolled bleeding: Apply pressure and call 911.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Confusion or disorientation, new: This may be a brain problem.
- Fall with an injury: Get checked out today.
- Severe pain that medicine does not help: Your pain needs managing.
- Sudden significant weight gain: Fluid may be building up.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that is slowly improving: You are healing well.
- Questions about a medicine or dose: Your nurse can help you.
- Wound healing slower than expected: Call us if it gets worse.
